page.layout: One printed page: running head at top centre with page number at top left; a full-width emblem heading; a woodcut engraving in the centre (a crucifixion beneath a tree, with kneeling figures); four lines of italic verse below the engraving; a catchword at the lower right.

p.i: [Woodcut engraving: Christ crucified on a tree, the titulus INRI above, with kneeling figures at the foot. Not text.]

l.i: Planicies Christus cæli est, atq; vmbra salutis.
Nec venit ex alio lux, via, vita, salus.

page.notes: The verse lines are centred and set in italic. The first line reads "præruptaviator" in the scan with the words run together; it is printed as "præruptaviator" with a probable space missing between "prærupta" and "viator", written as "prærupta viator" in the scan. The word "vitat" appears as printed. The third line ends with a dash-like mark after "salutis". The running head "EMBLEMA" is set in small capitals with the letter spacing of the printer. The catchword "Quod" is partly cut off at the right edge of the scan.
